title: Bonjour les couleurs!
oneGoal: Students recognize and name primary colors in their environment
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with French color words?
Do we need more visual cues or gestures?
Should we extend or shorten color hunt activity?
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces the magical world of colors that will be explored throughout the unit
realWorldConnection: Colors are everywhere - in our clothes, toys, nature, and food we see every day

title: Les couleurs ont des sentiments
oneGoal: Students connect primary colors to basic emotions and feelings
decisionPoints: Are students making personal connections to colors and feelings?
Do we need to model more emotional expressions?
Should we use more concrete examples from their experiences?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by connecting the named primary colors to how they make us feel inside
realWorldConnection: When we choose clothes or decorate our rooms, colors help show how we feel

title: Rouge comme...
oneGoal: Students explore red in nature and connect it to energy and warmth
decisionPoints: Are students finding red examples in their surroundings?
Do we need more scaffolding for descriptive language?
Should we incorporate movement to show energy?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by deeply exploring one primary color (red) and its emotional and natural connections
realWorldConnection: Red appears in stop signs, fire trucks, apples, and flowers - it gets our attention and shows importance

title: Bleu comme le ciel
oneGoal: Students discover blue in nature and connect it to peace and coolness
decisionPoints: Are students contrasting blue feelings with red from last lesson?
Do we need to go outside to observe blue in nature?
Should we incorporate calming movements or breathing?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by exploring blue as a contrast to red, showing how different colors create different moods
realWorldConnection: Blue sky makes us feel calm, blue water is refreshing, and blue pajamas help us feel peaceful at bedtime

title: Jaune comme le soleil
oneGoal: Students connect yellow to happiness and light
decisionPoints: Are students showing joy when working with yellow?
Do we need more examples of yellow bringing happiness?
Should we sing or move to express yellow's energy?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by completing the primary color exploration with yellow's bright, happy energy
realWorldConnection: Yellow sun makes us smile, yellow flowers brighten gardens, and yellow makes us think of fun times

title: Mélanges magiques: Rouge + Jaune
oneGoal: Students discover that mixing red and yellow creates orange
decisionPoints: Are students amazed by the color transformation?
Do we need more hands-on mixing time?
Should we predict what will happen before mixing?
progression: Builds on Lessons 3 and 5 by combining red and yellow knowledge to create the magic of color mixing
realWorldConnection: We mix ingredients when cooking, and colors mix too - like orange pumpkins and carrots in nature

title: Mélanges magiques: Bleu + Jaune
oneGoal: Students discover that mixing blue and yellow creates green
decisionPoints: Are students making connections to green in nature?
Do we need to explore more green examples around us?
Should we compare green feelings to primary colors?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by learning another color mixing combination and connecting green to the natural world
realWorldConnection: Green grass, leaves, and plants grow all around us - mixing colors helps us paint nature

title: Mélanges magiques: Rouge + Bleu
oneGoal: Students discover that mixing red and blue creates purple
decisionPoints: Are students intrigued by purple's special qualities?
Do we need examples of purple in their world?
Should we explore purple's mysterious feeling?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by completing the secondary color discoveries through mixing all primary combinations
realWorldConnection: Purple flowers are special, purple clothes feel fancy, and purple makes things seem magical

title: L'automne en couleurs
oneGoal: Students connect warm colors (red, orange, yellow) to autumn feelings and changes
decisionPoints: Are students observing autumn colors in their environment?
Do we need to collect real leaves for exploration?
Should we discuss why leaves change colors?
progression: Builds on Lessons 6-8 by applying color mixing knowledge to understand seasonal color patterns
realWorldConnection: Autumn leaves turn beautiful warm colors, and we can paint or draw these changes we see outside

title: L'hiver en couleurs
oneGoal: Students explore cool colors (blue, white, purple) and winter emotions
decisionPoints: Are students feeling the coolness of winter colors?
Do we need to contrast with warm autumn colors?
Should we incorporate winter experiences they know?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by contrasting seasonal colors and helping students see how colors reflect natural changes
realWorldConnection: Winter snow is white and blue, making us feel quiet and peaceful, different from autumn's energy

title: Couleurs dans ma famille
oneGoal: Students explore how different cultures use colors in celebrations and traditions
decisionPoints: Are students sharing their family's color traditions respectfully?
Do we need to provide examples from various cultures?
Should we create a visual display of diverse traditions?
progression: Builds on Lessons 9-10 by expanding color connections beyond seasons to cultural and family meanings
realWorldConnection: Families use special colors for holidays, celebrations, and traditions that are important to them

title: Mon arc-en-ciel d'émotions
oneGoal: Students create a personal color wheel connecting all colors to their own emotions
decisionPoints: Are students making personal connections to all colors learned?
Do we need to review color mixing before creating?
Should we allow individual interpretation of color feelings?
progression: Builds on all previous lessons by combining color knowledge with personal emotional connections
realWorldConnection: Everyone feels differently about colors based on their experiences and personality

title: Artistes et leurs couleurs
oneGoal: Students observe how famous artists use colors to express feelings and ideas
decisionPoints: Are students making connections between artist choices and emotions?
Do we need simpler art examples for this age?
Should we focus on one artist or show variety?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by showing how real artists use the same color principles students have learned
realWorldConnection: Artists throughout history have used colors to tell stories and share feelings, just like we do

title: Ma création colorée
oneGoal: Students demonstrate all color learning by creating their own expressive artwork
decisionPoints: Are students applying color mixing and emotional connections?
Do we need to provide choice in materials or subject?
Should we plan for sharing and celebration?
progression: Builds on all 13 previous lessons by allowing students to demonstrate their complete understanding of color magic
realWorldConnection: We can use everything we learned about colors to create art that shows who we are and how we feel

title: Couleurs dans notre école
oneGoal: Students practice color identification and mixing by exploring school environment
decisionPoints: Which areas of school offer the most color variety?
Are students applying learned vocabulary naturally?
Should we document findings for future reference?
progression: Extension: Applies all color knowledge in familiar school setting for reinforcement practice
realWorldConnection: School colors help us feel welcome and create a positive learning environment

title: Peinture libre avec couleurs chaudes
oneGoal: Students freely explore warm colors while practicing mixing and emotional expression
decisionPoints: Are students confidently mixing warm colors?
Do we need to encourage experimentation?
Should we play music to inspire warm color feelings?
progression: Extension: Deepens warm color exploration from Lesson 9 with open-ended creative practice
realWorldConnection: Warm colors help us feel cozy and energetic, perfect for decorating spaces where we want to feel happy

title: Peinture libre avec couleurs froides
oneGoal: Students freely explore cool colors while practicing mixing and calming expressions
decisionPoints: Are students experiencing the calming effect of cool colors?
Do we need quiet music or nature sounds?
Should we encourage slower, more meditative movements?
progression: Extension: Deepens cool color exploration from Lesson 10 with peaceful creative practice
realWorldConnection: Cool colors help us feel calm and peaceful, perfect for bedrooms or quiet spaces

title: Couleurs de nos jouets favoris
oneGoal: Students analyze and recreate colors from beloved toys and objects
decisionPoints: Are students excited to share their favorite objects?
Do we need help with color matching techniques?
Should we create a class gallery of favorite things?
progression: Extension: Applies color skills to personally meaningful objects for engaging practice
realWorldConnection: The colors of our favorite things often reflect our personality and what makes us happy

title: Histoire colorée en images
oneGoal: Students tell a story using only colors and simple shapes
decisionPoints: Are students connecting colors to story emotions effectively?
Do we need to scaffold storytelling structure?
Should we encourage peer sharing and interpretation?
progression: Extension: Combines all color emotional connections in creative storytelling practice
realWorldConnection: Colors help tell stories in books, movies, and art all around us every day

title: Célébration de nos couleurs magiques
oneGoal: Students celebrate their color journey by sharing favorite creations and discoveries
decisionPoints: How should students choose which work to share?
Do we invite families or other classes to celebrate?
Should we create a permanent display of their learning?
progression: Extension: Celebrates and reflects on the complete color learning journey with pride and joy
realWorldConnection: Artists share their work with others because art is meant to be enjoyed and celebrated together
